text: The Application Navigator is the panel pinned to the left edge of almost every classic and UI16 screen in ServiceNow. It's the primary way you find and launch every screen on the instance, and understanding its anatomy is the first real navigation skill any admin needs.

At the top sits a filter box, then a row of views: All, Favorites, and History — with Workspaces showing up too once your instance has them configured. Below that is a tree of applications, like Incident, Problem, Change, and Service Catalog. Expand an application and you'll find its modules underneath — the actual clickable screens, such as Create New, Open, and Assigned to me inside the Incident application. Most modules are really just saved links to a list view of a table with a particular filter already baked in.

There are three real ways to get around the navigator. Browse the All tree by hand when you're still learning what's installed on the instance — this teaches you the actual shape of the platform. Pin the modules you open constantly into Favorites using the star icon, so you stop re-expanding the same application every session. And let History do the remembering for you — it automatically tracks the last several modules and records you had open, which is often the fastest way back to something from five minutes ago.

Typing into the filter box narrows the whole tree live, matching application names and module names at the same time. But the fastest method of all skips the tree entirely: type a table name followed by ".list" — for example "incident.list" — and press Enter to jump straight to that table's list view, with no saved module required at all. The equivalent ".do" suffix opens a brand-new, blank form for that same table instead.

That direct-navigation shortcut works for any table you have permission to see, including tables that have no module pointing at them whatsoever — which is exactly why working admins reach for it constantly instead of hunting through menus. Next up: how this classic, general-purpose navigator compares to ServiceNow's newer, purpose-built workspaces.
